Let me think about the verifier more carefully to make sure my inputs produce correct outputs. The verifier:

- x0 = objects(I, T, F, F): univalued=True, diagonal=False, without_bg=False. So objects are connected components of same color (4-connectivity), bg=None so all colors counted.

Wait, with without_bg=False, bg=None, all cells are considered. Objects are connected same-colored regions.

- x1 = lbind(colorfilter, x0): filter objects by color.
- x2 = compose(size, x1): count objects of a given color.
- x3 = matcher(x2, ONE): colors that have exactly one object.
- x4 = palette(I): all colors.
- x5 = sfilter(x4, x3): colors that form exactly one connected component.
- x6 = fork(equality, toindices, box): objects whose indices equal their box (i.e., the object is a filled rectangle / box outline equals the whole object). Actually box gives outline; equality(toindices, box) means the object equals its bounding box outline. So object is exactly a rectangular ring (border).
- x7 = rbind(contained, x5): filter objects whose color is in x5.
- x8 = compose(x7, color): given object, check if its color is in x5.
- x9 = sfilter(x0, x8): objects with unique color.
- x10 = rbind(greater, SEVEN): size > 7.
- x11 = compose(x10, size): object has more than 7 cells.
- x12 = sfilter(x9, x11): unique color objects larger than 7 cells.
- x13 = extract(x12, x6): first object satisfying equality(indices, box).
- x14 = subgrid(x13, I): crop to bounding box.
- x15 = trim(x14): remove border.

So the rectangle is a border (hollow rectangle) of one color, whose border cells form the whole object. And its color appears only once as an object.

The interior can be any colors (multi-colored).
